title: Access
audience: For everyone: who may do what, on the logic panel and the three built admin screens.

sections.heading: Principles
lines: This page answers the 7 Oct 2026 call: "what kind of roles, what kind of access, what kind of permissions".
A few people (7 Oct 2026 call): two working roles, the Principal officer and the Logic analyst, plus Compliance and Read only. At launch, two people run the panel; one of them can send.
Ten fixed roles; no one can make a new one. A person holds one or more, and no one gets rights outside their roles.
Two people on every sent change, whatever roles they hold: the author never does the second check, and only the Principal officer sends. The one exception: an urgent hold (see Approval).
The server checks the role on every request and every change; the screen only mirrors it. A greyed-out button is never the real check.
Everything is logged, refused attempts too. Sent changes and saved copies are never edited; a fix is a new record.

sections.heading: The roles
lines: Principal officer: the only role that sends a change. Also manages staff and roles.
Logic analyst: edits the rules in drafts and tests them.
Compliance: signs Assumptions and Risk scores changes before they are sent, and is told of every other change as it goes out.
A new working role starts only once Compliance signs it: proposed (LQ42).
Adviser takes calls, Call centre works the call tasks, Support answers tickets.
Ops: adds facts to the unknown funds list (L04b) and queues each sent change's email in {I14}.
Read only: product and tech sit here. Reads, never changes anything.
Marketing and Finance: no access to the logic panel; their admin screen rights are in the table by screen.
In the examples, staff are named by role and number (Principal officer 01, Logic analyst 01); no real person is drawn.

sections.heading: What each role may do, by screen
lines: Built from the screens files, so it is never typed twice. First every Logic tab screen in order, variants included: the role and writes fields of data/logic_screens.json. Then M03, M07 and M10, as they stand in data/admin_screens.json.
Cells: act (the role makes changes there; the Writes column says which), read, none, and "-" where the admin screen does not name the role.
"read, own people" ("own" for short): the role reads its own clients only. "read masked": it reads with client names left out. The table by action calls them "read, own clients" and "read, no names".
On L02, L03, L14, L04, L09, L07 and their variants, read for Adviser, Call centre, Ops and Support means the rules in use and their reasons only; draft rows are not sent to them.
On L08 the Logic analyst sees the sent changes and the versions plans are on, not the log. On L13, the staff list and the roles table, not the access checks.
The Writes column lists each write in the screens file's words: the action (its event; the roles that may do it).

lines: A draft goes: open, checked, trial run done, waiting for a second check, approved, sent. Sent back, it is open again. A draft can also be discarded.
To be decided: which other changes Compliance must sign (LQ45).
The second check covers the changes, how it reaches plans and the reason clients read. Changing any of them after approval sends it back.

The urgent path: an urgent hold by the Principal officer alone folds steps 1 to 8 into one action. Besides the hold, it may carry only the fund basket split needed to pass the safety limits (L09). Compliance is told at once.

A second person, not the one who placed it, signs it off within two working days. If not, it stays in force, shown as overdue on L08, L10 and L11 (LQ30). The Logic analyst may only ask for one (LQ25).
With two people at launch, every sent change needs both, except an urgent hold. To be decided: what happens when the Principal officer is away (LQ7).
The 7 Oct 2026 call asked for this step-by-step flow. Its nine steps were set while building, in the logic plan of 8 Oct 2026, and are open to veto.

lines: A log line: who, role, when, what, before, after, reason. A refused attempt is a line too, marked as refused (L08).
The Principal officer and Compliance read and export the log; Read only reads it; the Logic analyst does not see it.

The access check covers each person's roles, status (active, suspended or revoked), who added them and when, last sign-in, and whether two-step sign-in is on. At launch a list and the log serve; the screen can follow.
In the examples, access check 1 on 15 Jul 2027 suspended Adviser 06, idle 90 days.
To be decided: the idle timeout, one session at a time, how old the security check may be (LQ41).

sections.heading: The client app
lines: The app has one kind of user, the client. What a client can do depends on their tier: what they are entitled to, not a role. Each board screen already shows it (LQ40).
The logic panel never answers a request carrying a client's token. It is a separate staff web app, desktop only (as on the board's L01), kept apart by its own web address and the type of token.
